charts.qrWarning: NASA released these photos in two batches, processed differently. Don't compare small brightness changes between one batch and the other.

measuredVs.consistent: The measurement landed {offset} arcseconds from the prediction, inside the margin of {margin}.
measuredVs.marginal: The measurement landed {offset} arcseconds from the prediction, outside the margin of {margin}, but not by enough to say they differ.
measuredVs.deviates: The measurement landed {offset} arcseconds from the prediction, far outside the margin of {margin}. That alone does not say which one is off.
measuredVs.inconsistent: The measurement landed {offset} arcseconds from the prediction, far outside the margin of {margin}. That alone does not say which one is off.

variability.varied: {band}: the brightness spread over {spread} magnitudes, more than the measurement errors explain.
variability.hint: {band}: the brightness spread over {spread} magnitudes, a little more than the errors predict. It may have changed, but this is not enough to say so.
variability.indicative: {band}: the brightness seems to spread over {spread} magnitudes, but these measurements are weak (too bright, too few or too noisy), so it may not be real.
variability.none: No change beyond what the measurement errors allow.
variability.more: {n, plural, one {# other colour shows} other {# other colours show}} something similar.

charts.tapHint: Tap a dot to read it
charts.outside: {n, plural, one {# dot} other {# dots}} beyond this frame
charts.batchNote: Photos from two NASA batches: small brightness differences between them may not be real.

info.spectrumDot: Each dot is one SPHEREx measurement in one colour of infrared light. The bar shows how uncertain it is.
info.hollow: A hollow dot means the object was too bright there, so the value is approximate.
info.spectrumAxes: From left to right the wavelength grows, in micrometres (µm): the left is closer to the light we see, the right closer to heat. Brightness is in millijanskys (mJy), a unit astronomers use.
info.logScale: The brightness scale goes up in steps of 10 times.
info.lightcurveDot: Each dot is the brightness measured in one pass, in one SPHEREx colour. The bar shows how uncertain it is.
info.magnitudeScale: Magnitude is the astronomers' brightness scale: a lower number means brighter, so brighter is at the top.
info.motionMarks: The cross is where the catalogue predicts the object. The dots are where SkySwap measured it in SPHEREx photos.
info.motionRing: The ring is the margin of error of this comparison. A measurement inside the ring agrees with the prediction.
info.motionLine: The line links the prediction to the measurement the sentence under the chart talks about.
info.arcsec: Distances are in arcseconds, a very small angle: one degree split into 3,600 parts. One SPHEREx pixel is {size} arcseconds.
info.pathView: Path puts both on the sky, counted from the first predicted position.

help.title: How to look
help.lookBody: A spot that shows up somewhere else in each photo. Stars stay still.
help.answerBody: Tap a button or swipe the photo: right is Yes, left is No, up is Not sure.
help.betterBody: Hold the photo to stop it. Let go to continue. Tap twice to zoom in.
help.defectBody: A spot that shows up in one photo only is usually a camera defect.
help.emptyBody: Most cards have nothing new. Answering that nothing moved helps too.
help.blackBody: Black along the edge: the telescope did not photograph this part. A star with a black center: it is too bright for the camera. This is normal.

tools.diffNote: Still stars also become a bright and dark pair.

result.label: Result
result.movesOkPlain: You got it: it's a moving object
result.movesWrongPlain: It did move: it's a moving object
result.defectWrong: It didn't move: it's a photo defect
result.bodyMovesOk: It shows up somewhere else in each photo. The green diamond shows where.
result.bodyMovesWrong: Look again: it shows up somewhere else in each photo.
result.bodyDefect: The spot shows up in one photo only. It is usually a particle hitting the camera.
result.bodyTrail: It is a line across the photo. It is usually a passing satellite or a camera defect.
result.bodyStill: All the stars stayed where they were. Most cards are like this.

understand.title: Understand this card
understand.whyMoves: Stars always stay in the same place. An asteroid is closer to us and travels between one photo and the next.
understand.whyDefect: What is real shows up in almost every photo. What shows up only once is usually a defect.
understand.whyStill: Almost no card has anything new. Answering that nothing moved helps the research too.

welcome.body2: Stars stay still. Asteroids and comets change place.

stack.title: Follow a motion
stack.body: Adds up all the photos in this colour, shifted along a straight path you set. A faint star moving that way gets brighter. Fast asteroids cross the photo in hours, so this tool can't follow them.

settings.title: Settings
settings.dataBody: SkySwap shows real images from NASA's SPHEREx telescope, kept in a public NASA archive. Infrared light is shown in grey, and any colour you see is false colour. The sky index lists {images} published images, so any spot can be opened. Spots with many photos can take a few seconds the first time; after that they are kept in the browser. Data kit {version}.
settings.about: SkySwap is a non-commercial study prototype for the NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge "Planet X and SPHEREx". It is not affiliated with NASA or Instagram.
settings.notesCount: {n, plural, =0 {No notes saved} one {# note saved} other {# notes saved}}
settings.loggedOut: Pick a nickname to keep your progress.
settings.creditOn: On: your nickname shows on findings.
settings.creditOff: Off: you show as anonymous on findings.
settings.logoutBody: There is no password, so you can't come back to this nickname. Your answers stay counted, and your private notes stay in this browser.

marking.yellowBody: Where star catalogues say this object should be on this date. It is a calculation, not a measurement.
marking.youBody: Where you saw it. The cross stays hidden while you mark, so it cannot influence you.
marking.othersBody: The average of everyone who marked this post. You only see it after marking.
marking.whyBody: The cross is a calculation and can be wrong. Your mark shows where a person really sees the object. If many people mark far from the cross, that is a sign it is worth checking.
marking.whyHonest: For now, marks appear here to compare. They do not yet count toward the answer to "Did anything move?".
marking.resultTitle: {n, plural, one {# photo marked} other {# photos marked}}
marking.resultGap: Typically {pct}% of the photo's width from the yellow cross. Bright stars are wide and tap targets are big, so small gaps are normal.

meIntro.title: How your profile works
meIntro.lead: Points, levels and badges only mark your path. What helps is your answers.
meIntro.helpBody: Practice sets with a known answer show how far to trust your eyes. After that, your answers change the chance that something moves.
meIntro.pointsBody: Answer: 2. Mark a post: 5. Tag or follow: 1. Any answer earns the same, so there is no need to guess.
meIntro.levelsBody: {ladder}. They never drop and unlock nothing.
meIntro.badgesBody: Tap one to see how to earn it. Some give 10 points. Exploring ones are just for fun.
meIntro.daysBody: Your first action of the day adds 5, then 10 the next day, up to 30. Miss a day and the count restarts. You keep your points.
meIntro.limitsBody: Up to {cap} points a day. Past the limits your answers still count. Only the points stop.

community.lead: Every item came from people's blind answers. A candidate is not a discovery until someone checks it.
community.exampleNotice: This is an example for testing. It is not a real finding.
community.foundByAnonymous: Found by {n, plural, one {# anonymous person} other {# anonymous people}}
community.firstVote: First answer that saw it move, by {name}
community.firstVoteAnonymous: First answer that saw it move

checks.gaia: Fast stars in Gaia, moved to this date

community.namingNote: If confirmed, the object gets a catalogue name and credit for those who found it, not the right to name it.
community.emptyBody: A patch of sky appears here when at least 5 careful answers agree that something moves. Your answers help get there.

candidate.label: Candidate
candidate.body: Careful answers say something moves here. Nobody has confirmed it.

known.label: Matches a known object
known.body: An automatic check matched this spot to {name}, already in the catalogues. That shows the method works, so your answers counted.

likely_artifact.label: Probably a glitch
likely_artifact.body: Careful answers now say nothing moves here. Your answers counted.

package_ready.label: Ready to check
package_ready.body: It passed the automatic checks. Nobody has reviewed it yet.

in_review.label: In review
